spec.title: Course Schedule
spec.summary: Courses are numbered from zero through numCourses minus one.
spec.description: Courses are numbered from zero through numCourses minus one. For each prerequisite pair [course, prerequisite], the second course must be taken before the first. Return whether some ordering lets you finish every course; a dependency cycle makes this impossible. Courses with no listed prerequisite still count.

examples.explanation: Every course in the cycle waits on another.

approaches.name: Remove Available Courses
approaches.summary: Repeatedly take courses with no remaining prerequisites and remove their outgoing dependencies.
thinkingSteps: Count prerequisites for each course and build outgoing edges.
Queue every course with count zero.
Process the queue and check whether all courses were taken.

bullets: A course can be taken only after its prerequisites.
A cycle leaves no available starting course.
Independent courses should also be counted.

approaches.name: Detect a Dependency Cycle
approaches.summary: Traverse prerequisites while tracking the current recursion path; any back-edge prevents completion.
thinkingSteps: Build a graph from courses to their prerequisites.
Mark nodes on the current path separately from completed nodes.
Reject a repeated node on the current path; otherwise finish every component.

bullets: A circular prerequisite chain is impossible.
A course may have several paths leading to it.
